source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: DartPoints operates its Shreveport, Louisiana data center at 601 Milam Street, notable among all of DartPoints' facilities for being explicitly marketed as Uptime Institute Tier III-rated, described on DartPoints' own site as the only Tier III-rated data center in Louisiana and the 46th facility to receive that certification nationally, the only building in this entire research batch to carry a disclosed Tier rating. This facility traces its origin to Venyu, a company DartPoints describes as having operated for more than 30 years as Louisiana's premier data center infrastructure and cloud services provider, acquired by DartPoints on May 2, 2023 from its then-parent company REV, itself formed through a 2019 merger of the Louisiana telecom cooperatives RTC and EATEL. Per DartPoints' own acquisition announcement, the Shreveport facility was constructed to US Department of Defense anti-terrorism force protection codes, described as one of the nation's most secure commercial data centers. The facility spans a 5,600-square-foot data hall supporting more than 200 active racks at densities up to 20 kilowatts per rack, drawing 2.2 megawatts of utility power against a 0.9-megawatt critical IT load, backed by 4,000 kilowatts of generator capacity and cooled by 760 tons of capacity, with 9 on-site network providers. DartPoints publishes a customer case study describing Origin Bank, a regional bank operating across five states and 60 locations, as a Shreveport customer since 2013 using the facility as its primary colocation environment, one of the more specific tenant references found in this entire research session, unusual given the industry's general practice of not disclosing colocation tenants. As is standard industry practice for most other DartPoints customers, further tenant identities are not publicly disclosed.

reading.body:
DartPoints Shreveport operates 2.2 MW of published IT capacity in downtown Shreveport, translating to roughly 55 racks at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack.

The facility is one of three data centers for which DartPoints acquired underlying real estate in April 2025, when NOVA Infrastructure took majority control of the operator with over 250 million dollars in committed growth capital. DartPoints runs 11 facilities across 10 regional markets in tier-2 and tier-3 United States metros, serving more than 900 enterprise customers. The company markets itself on AI-ready, high-density infrastructure with 99.999 percent uptime and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This Shreveport node is the third largest by published capacity in Louisiana, accounting for one of 7.7 MW across the four facilities mapped in the state.

The facility represents the regional colocation tier rather than hyperscaler infrastructure. It offers fixed capacity to enterprise tenants, universities, and hospital systems rather than operating as an AI-native platform. At 2.2 MW, it sits well outside the scale that shapes national AI compute constraints, though it may serve local enterprise and university demand for managed infrastructure.

The data published does not cover local power availability, grid constraints, planned capacity expansion, or utilization rates at this address. DartPoints' strategy targets communities outside major metros, but whether Shreveport's grid can support significant expansion remains undocumented.
